answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce location-bound identities via radio multilateration. Beacons across a subarctic tundra, a major river, and an offshore island emit nanosecond challenges that nodes must echo. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of deploying dedicated physical transceivers in separate spatial cells per identity. However, multipath reflections and weather variations can distort signal timing, occasionally rejecting legitimate nodes.
